Subject (in full) Soviet Interest in China Revived.

Made by D.S. Maklansky. Forwarded by Phil Robertson C.D.I.

With reference to attached newspaper article of
April 1, 1930 from the Shanghai Times, careful enquiries
have failed to find any corroborations of this report,
nor have any rumours been in circulation in Shanghai.
to the effect that Soviet specialists experienced in
Chinese revolutionary affairs have again been sent to
the East.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
The Shanghai Evening Post, Monday, April 21, 1930

Travel
School To Leave
Seattle June 15

An Oriental travel school is being
sponsored by the Dollar Steamship
Company. Comprising American
teachers and students, an educa-
tional cruise will start at Seattle
June 15. The group will tour China,
Japan and the Philippines.

Dollar officials announce that
they have engaged Professor V. E.
Froula, principal of Roosevelt High
School of Seattle, to lead the
students on their tour.

The travellers will use various
ships of the Dollar Line on the trip.
Sailing from Seattle aboard the
President Pierce, they will proceed
to Yokohama. A study then will
be made of Japan and her cities,
after which the party will sail for
China. Peiping, Tientsin, Shang-
hai, Nanking, Hongkong and Can-
ton are Chinese cities at which the
group will call.

Lasting more than two months,
the cruise will end at Seattle on
August 29 when the party will re-
turn to that port on the President
McKinley. Members of the group
who wish may return to San Fran-
cisco via Honolulu will end their
trip September 3.

The cost for each member of the
party will be $1,318. This will
include all transportation and meals
during the tour. Hotel expenses,
baggage transportation and guides
also are included.

Reg,
Please file
